owner: CC owns the code, the proof and the probe. Akien owns nothing here that needs his gate: the refusal's existence follows from Law 7 and from host.py's own filed edge, and no spec choice is at issue.
children: none, because the seam is one function (host.py:_post, ~14 lines) plus its proof, and the one thing that could have been a child — the host-side cause of the wedge — is explicitly out of scope and is not a code-seam at all (nothing on this box is edited to fix it).

questions.a: DETECTION IS NOT THE DEFECT — THE NAME IS. metered_cost already refuses correctly and must keep refusing; its job is pricing and it is right to decline to price an answerless response. What it cannot do is say WHY, because by the time it sees the payload the HTTP status and the raw body are gone. The refusal belongs where both are in scope, which is _post and nowhere else.

THE THREE TELLS, so the check is not 'content is empty': `done` is FALSE (a finished non-streaming response is always true), `done_reason` is ABSENT, and the counters are absent — on top of an empty message and a zero-valued `model` and `created_at`. A legitimately empty completion has done true, a done_reason, and counters. Building the check on the empty content alone is the coin-toss-red version of this ticket.

WHAT WEDGES AND WHAT CLEARS THE HOST IS UNMEASURED, n=1 on the transition. Observed: while wedged, every request returns the zero value instantly, including a one-message request; after a streaming request and some minutes, everything passed including the full payload. Whether the stream request cleared it, whether time did, or whether something else did, is not known — and the hex-side ollama log was never read. Deliberately out of scope: the seam-side refusal is buildable and provable without it, and bundling an unbounded host investigation into a code-seam is how a ticket stops being finishable. Recorded so it is a known unknown rather than a silence.

THIS CAST IS A DECLINED REACH, DONE PROPERLY. aider_shim charter edge (o) records the same measurement from the consumer's side and explicitly refuses to edit inference_domain's code from another component's voyage (Law 6: the owner alone gates writes). The ticket is what that refusal is supposed to produce.

workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> [SUPERSEDED] -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(host_empty_answer_refusal) -> PROVED

watchme.trigger: every host call that raises the new refusal, and every call that raises HostUnmetered — both, because the pair is the measurement: the watch is answering whether the split actually SPLIT anything, and one arm alone cannot say.
watchme.enough: when 10 refusals have been recorded across the two arms and every one is on the arm its body warrants (an answerless 200 on the new arm, a counterless-but-answered response on HostUnmetered), or when any single misfiling appears — the first misfiling is the finding and stops the watch immediately, because it means the split is drawn in the wrong place.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier, carrying the raised class and the raw body's key set for each recorded refusal
watchme.nexus: the inference_domain trouble/verdict record — the same surface that carries host.py's filed edges
watchme.consumer: whoever next reads a drive record that names an unheard ask; today that is aider_shim's driver, whose DriveRefused message quotes the fence's dispositions verbatim

intent_berth: none, because this entered at the TICKET door, not the INTENT door: it is a bug, and editing lines of code in cairn/devices/inference_domain/host.py:_post fixes it — no harmony of the system is broken and no intention was implemented contrary to its actual intention. /intent's charter (skills/intent/SKILL.md) names TICKET as one of the three entry points and directs bugs away from the birth questions explicitly.
